anomalies.observed: R34 is valued 120k, but it is a CAN termination resistor between /CAN0_N and the SW6 DIP switch. Its sibling R35 on CAN1 is 120R. R34 is also built from the same 120R-coded part (MPN 0603WAF1200T5E, footprint MotorController:TAYLOR_RESISTOR) as R35, so the 120k value does not match its part.
anomalies.expected: A 120 ohm CAN bus termination resistor, matching R35 and the CAN termination role. A 120k value would leave CAN0 effectively unterminated and would break reliable communication with the Odrive controllers.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (`CAN0`, `CAN1`), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller

anomalies.impact: CAN0 would have a near-open termination, causing signal reflections and reduced bus reliability on the CAN0 link to the motor controllers, and possibly bit errors.

anomalies.observed: The P-channel ideal-diode FET Q1 has its source (pin 2) on +5V and its drain (pin 3) on USBC_VBUS_IN. The LTC4412 VIN pin (U6.1) is on USBC_VBUS_IN and SENSE (U6.6) is on +5V. The other P-channel load switches (Q6, Q9) use source on +5V and drain on the load. The FET is therefore oriented in reverse relative to the input and sense connections.
anomalies.expected: For an LTC4412 ideal-diode OR-ing stage, the P-FET source should be on the input (VBUS) and the drain on the +5V load, so that the body diode and channel only pass current from VBUS to +5V and block reverse current. The note asks for reverse-current protection.

evidence.quote: Q1 | Q_PMOS_GSD | Package_TO_SOT_SMD:SOT-23 | Device:Q_PMOS_GSD | P-MOSFET transistor, gate/source/drain
USBC_VBUS_IN [High Power] : J3.A4(VBUS,passive) J3.A9(VBUS,passive) J3.B4(VBUS,passive) J3.B9(VBUS,passive) Q1.3(D,passive) R11.1(passive) R64.2(2,passive) U25.5(VBUS,passive) U6.1(VIN,power_in)

anomalies.impact: Reverse current can flow from the +5V rail back into the USB input through the FET body diode, so the intended reverse-current protection and ideal-diode power path would not work as designed.

anomalies.observed: The second LED channel of dual LED D30 has its anode (D30.4, A2) on ESTOP_OUT, and its cathode (D30.2, K2) returns through R60 to ESTOP_OUT as well. Both ends of that LED path sit on the same net, so the channel is shorted and carries no current. The other channel's resistor R59 returns to GND (R59.2 is in the GND net), but R60 does not.
anomalies.expected: R60 should return the LED cathode to GND like its counterpart R59, so the e-stop status LED can light from the ESTOP_OUT drive.

evidence.quote: ESTOP_OUT : D30.4(A2,input) J13.6(Pin_6,passive) J2.6(Pin_6,passive) R60.2(passive) U36.4(Y,output)

anomalies.impact: The e-stop indicator LED channel never lights. The design also leaves a logically meaningless loop on the e-stop output net. This does not directly affect the e-stop function itself.

parsed.summary: The most likely anomaly is R34, a CAN0 termination resistor whose value is 120k where its CAN1 counterpart R35 is 120R and both use the same 120R-coded part. The Q1 source/drain orientation in the USB ideal-diode path and the shorted D30 LED channel are lower-confidence additional findings.
